decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up right-arm approach toward the visible key; keep left arm parked and grippers open.
Continue a smooth elbow-up arc, pitching the right gripper downward toward the key.
Advance above the right-side key while matching its observed heading; maintain gradual joint changes.
Bring the right link6 above the key for a downward pinch, then inspect wrist alignment before closing.
Fine-align the key shaft with the right wrist center using small lateral corrections; keep jaws open.
Pinch the centered key shaft just above its bow; retention will be checked during a small lift.
Allow the right pinch to settle, then start lifting without changing the key heading.
Lift the visually retained key clear of the tabletop, keeping the right gripper closed.
Raise and rotate the retained key toward a central handoff pose, keeping the right arm in its workspace.
Continue the gradual handoff rotation and lift; the key remains visible between the right jaws.
Move the held key closer to the handoff area while rotating its bow toward the left hand.
Finish presenting the key horizontally at the handoff height, with the bow accessible from the left.
Hold the key steady in the right hand and initiate an elbow-up left-arm approach for the handoff.
Continue the left elbow-up arc toward the key bow, keeping clear of the stationary right gripper.
Advance the left hand through a continuous elbow-up arc, rotating its open jaws toward the exposed bow.
Approach the handoff from the left, gradually leveling the gripper with the bow while retaining the key in the right hand.
Level the left hand beside the key bow and partially narrow its jaws before the final handoff approach.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller rotation increments, then partially close the left jaws beside the bow.
Approach the exposed key bow slowly, lowering the left pinch to its observed height while the right hand retains it.
Make a small height correction at the handoff while approaching the bow; verify alignment before closing.
Center the bow between the left jaws and begin the receiving pinch while the right hand continues holding.
Complete and settle the left receiving pinch without moving either arm; retain right grip until the bow is secured.
Transfer support to the left bow pinch by gradually opening the stationary right gripper; inspect retention before separating.
The key slipped during transfer. Withdraw the empty left hand and lower the open right hand for a controlled recovery.
Lower the open right gripper above the dropped key, keeping the left hand clear for a second pickup.
Recenter the dropped key under the open right jaws, matching its changed heading while descending cautiously.
Refine the recovery alignment from the right wrist image: straighten the key shaft and place its lower section within the pinch.
Correct the recovery approach using both views; move toward the bow and rotate to the key's current tabletop direction.
Attempt a recovery pinch on the lower shaft with a small camera-guided translation; avoid further tabletop rotation.
Settle the recovery pinch and begin a small lift to determine whether the key is retained.
Lift the recovered key and begin returning it to a clearer handoff pose; keep the receiving hand open.
Restore a level, elevated handoff presentation and raise the receiving pinch to the bow plane.
Raise the held bow to the receiving-hand height and narrow the left jaws in preparation for a better-centered transfer.
Advance the left jaws around the bow with only a small height correction, keeping the donor hand fixed.
Advance the centered bow farther between the left finger pads, then close gently while retaining donor support.
Secure the centered bow in the left pinch, then gradually release the right fingers without moving the arms.
Finish opening the donor hand and separate it rightward; inspect that the key remains with the closed left hand.
Confirm the key remains in the left pinch while moving the open right hand fully clear of the transfer area.
The key is retained by the left hand. Begin its pose-adjustment arc toward an upright insertion orientation.
Rotate the left-held key toward vertical through small continuous increments, lifting it clear of the lock before alignment.
Resume from the interrupted pose with smaller angular increments, maintaining the left key pinch and elbow-up continuity.
Raise and rotate the retained key toward upright above the left-side lock, adapting its heading to the visible slot.
Continue the smaller upright-orientation increments while positioning the left-held key above the visible lock.
Finish leveling the key shaft vertically over the lock, retaining clearance for visual slot alignment.
Adjust the upright key heading to the visible slot and lower slightly while preserving clearance for lateral alignment.
Use a small lateral correction to bring the visible slot under the upright key without descending into the lock yet.
Bring the slot center toward the visible key tip using the measured wrist-view response; keep insertion height fixed.
Make a millimeter-scale centering correction and begin a slow vertical insertion with the left gripper closed.
Correct the remaining side-to-side slot offset while lowering only a few millimeters, watching for accurate entry.
Nudge the key toward the remaining visible slot edge and continue a very slow insertion, keeping orientation fixed.
Relieve apparent rim contact with a small lift, then adjust fore-aft alignment before another controlled insertion.
Align the circular opening with the key tip and refine the slot heading at clearance before descending again.
Refine the blade-to-slot angular alignment while the circular opening is centered under the tip; maintain clearance.
Lower the aligned blade toward the slot in small increments, with a slight lateral centering correction.
Lift clear of the rim and correct the remaining visible blade-to-slot heading mismatch before inserting deeper.
Use millimeter-scale fore-aft and lateral corrections to place the blade tip directly at the circular slot opening.
Correct the visible slot-angle mismatch in the opposite direction while holding the blade clear of the rim.
With the slot now nearly parallel to the blade, make a final small yaw correction and descend slowly into the opening.
Continue the slow straight insertion now that the blade remains centered and stable against the slot opening.
Relieve the small insertion resistance and adjust a few millimeters along the slot before retrying; retain the bow firmly.
Seat the centered key a little deeper, then begin a small test turn while maintaining its upright position.
